steps.name: Pathway enrichment: fgsea on human orthologs + zebrafish-native GO
caveats: Ortholog mapping from zebrafish to human is lossy: genes without a clean one-to-one ortholog are dropped from the Hallmark analysis, and this can systematically exclude fish-specific or duplicated-gene-family loci (zebrafish underwent a teleost-specific genome duplication, so many human genes have 2+ zebrafish paralogs, complicating one-to-one mapping).
The zebrafish-native GO path (goseq/org.Dr.eg.db) avoids the ortholog loss but has substantially thinner functional annotation than human GO, especially for less-studied genes.
Enrichment results depend on the method; report both paths and their overlap/disagreement rather than treating either as definitive.
steps.context: Reference data available: MSigDB Hallmark human gene sets (GMT), WikiPathways human/mouse/rat GMTs (none for zebrafish), org.Dr.eg.db Bioconductor annotation package for zebrafish gene ID/GO mapping, and babelgene (CRAN) for ortholog mapping. No curated zebrafish pathway collection (MSigDB, WikiPathways, Reactome GMT) exists in the reference store, so cross-species mapping to human is required for MSigDB Hallmark; org.Dr.eg.db is used natively for zebrafish GO as an unmapped-organism check.

plan.title: Zebrafish larvae drug exposure DE + pathway analysis
plan.analytical_narrative: Three treated vs three control zebrafish larvae pools with raw gene-level Salmon counts (12000 genes x 6 samples; Ensembl Danio rerio annotation) are analyzed with the DESeq2 workflow grounded by the Inflexa knowledge service for a 3-vs-3, single-batch, unpaired bulk RNA-seq design. Step 1 checks sample structure (blind VST, PCA, sample-distance heatmap, library sizes) to catch outliers or unexpected clustering before any test runs. Step 2 fits DESeq2 (minimal pre-filter, median-of-ratios normalization inside the model, explicit reference level = control, Wald test, apeglm shrinkage, BH-adjusted independent filtering at alpha 0.05) and reports the p-value histogram, MA plot, dispersion plot, and the count of genes flagged NA by the Cook's-distance outlier rule — with an explicit power caveat because n=3/group finds only a minority of true effects, skewed toward large fold changes. Step 3 takes the full ranked gene list (Wald statistic, as stated per the disputed-metric rule) and runs fgsea preranked GSEA. Because Danio rerio has no curated MSigDB/WikiPathways collection in the reference store, genes are mapped to human orthologs (babelgene, one-to-one only) for MSigDB Hallmark human enrichment, with a zebrafish-native org.Dr.eg.db GO analysis run in parallel via goseq (with a length-bias offset, since goseq needs one) as a species-native cross-check; both the ortholog-mapping loss and the GO thinness limitation are stated in the report. Step 4 assembles the full report per the reporting rules: reproducibility record, effect-size table (unshrunken and shrunken LFC + SE), enrichment table with database/version/rank metric/universe/size window, leading-edge genes, and the annotation/ortholog-mapping caveats for a non-human/mouse organism.
